text:
incidents-bot: PAGING — control-plane error spike (5xx/timeouts) observed for auth.org-lookup and billing-config services. Error rate >15% over 2m. Pager: @luis. Severity: P2. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/controlplane-deps

luis: seeing a lot of 502s from gateway -> auth-orglookup fanout. Confirming which deploys hit production in the last 15m.

marta: I pushed a small config rollback to config-service ~10m ago for feature flags. Could be related. rolling it back now to test.

ashwin: traffic graph from grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/abc shows latency spike and a downstream 504s to billing API.

kevin: adding: sentry shows token validation timeouts in auth during JWT refresh path. May be a semantic change in config that altered cache TTLs.

luis: copying logs from gateway -> auth: ```
2026-03-15T14:00:03Z gateway ERROR upstream response 502 from auth.svc: timeout after 8s
2026-03-15T14:00:07Z gateway WARN retrying request route=org-lookup user=svc-agent
```

sre-bot: Attached trace: https://tracing/redwood/trace/0a1b2c showing tail of KV lookup and blocking call to billing.

marta: rollback complete for config-service (reverted template v20260315-1012). Observability: starting to re-evaluate caches.

ashwin: after rollback, initial error rate dropped to ~9% but still elevated. Some requests still hitting old route due to sticky connections.

kevin: suggestion: enable auth fallback to token-cache-only path for 5m and reduce org-lookup fanout concurrency to 4 to avoid thundering herd. Anyone object?

product-ops: customer impact: frontend errors and some failed org invites reported. CS already triaging top customers and adding notes.

luis: executing mitigation: 1) set env AUTH_TOKEN_CACHE_ONLY=true via runtime feature flag, 2) throttle org-lookup concurrency from 20 -> 4. Applying now.

marta: applying throttle via /config/patch: ```json
{"org_lookup_concurrency":4}
```

luis: feature flag applied, concurrency updated. Observability shows drop in upstream 502s within 30s.

ashwin: metrics: error rate now 2.1% and p95 latency down from 1.6s to 430ms. Good signal.

kevin: rolling emergency rollback for the billing-config change that introduced a blocking call to billing.svc in the hot path. Triggering release revert ID: r-2026-315-emerg.

marta: revert deployed to canary -> prod. Waiting for sync.

incidents-bot: NOTE: deployment r-2026-315-emerg rolled to prod at 14:42:11Z. Link: https://deploys/redwood/r-2026-315-emerg

sre-bot: synthetic checks: /health across regions showing nominal. Samples: eu-west 200 OK, us-east 200 OK.

luis: quick customer impact summary for pager handoff: - Duration of elevated 5xx: ~34 minutes - Affected endpoints: /v1/auth refresh, /v1/orgs/lookup - Customer visible: some org invite fails, SDK retries surfaced as increased latency - Estimated affected requests: ~18k, errors ~3k - Mitigation: config rollback + token-cache fallback + concurrency throttle.

product-ops: adding to post-incident notes and notifying support. Will coordinate comms for impacted customers tomorrow.

kevin: follow-up items: 1) add unit test for billing client to prevent blocking network calls on hot path, 2) add circuit-breaker for org-lookup, 3) improve deploy gating for config-service.

marta: creating a ticket: ENG-4387 with rollout timeline, revert diff, and instructions to reproduce locally.

luis: handing off to SRE rotation (ashwin) for monitoring and postmortem. Oncall shift ends in 45m. If anything regresses, page me again.

ashwin: ack, I'll monitor dashboards and set an alert threshold lower for next 24h. Also will capture flamegraphs from auth for the last hour.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — mitigation applied and error rates returned to baseline. Closing pager, but thread remains open for postmortem notes.

marta: leaving a short changelog entry in the repo and will attach the config diff to ENG-4387.

product-ops: CS note: two paying customers saw invite failures, logged individually. We'll send a targeted followup once postmortem complete. :handshake:

ashwin: prepping initial timeline for postmortem: will include detection timeline, config change list, mitigation steps, metrics before/after, and suggested permanent fixes.

luis: thanks team. Good triage and quick rollback. Closing my pager.

kevin: quick ack. We'll schedule a short blameless review tomorrow. :thumbsup:
